How often Editrove updates feeds, widgets, topic alerts and breaking news in the background. More frequent refreshes keep everything newer but use more battery and data. Android may stretch the interval when battery saver is on or the phone is idle.
Heads-up alerts when a newsroom you follow breaks a story: labelled “Breaking”, or minutes old and already carried by many outlets. Separate from topic alerts.
Checked on every background refresh (%1$s). For faster alerts, refresh every 15 or 30 minutes.
Split view keeps the feed and the story side by side. Full view uses the whole screen for each page, and stories open as full pages.

One JSON file with your topics, edition, sources and paywall rules. It also imports backups exported from the OpenWire web app.
Reset topics, edition, sources, paywall rules and preferences? Saved stories are kept.
A fast, ad-free and tracking-free news reader with a paywall-routing engine. No accounts, no analytics, no server of its own — your settings and saved stories never leave this device.

Editrove — editorial judgment meets a trove of stories. Editrove began as a fork of the original OpenWire web app by Anson Lai, whose paywall engine, source catalog and feed pipeline it ports and builds on.

Typefaces: Newsreader, Inter and JetBrains Mono (SIL Open Font License). Briefing music: royalty-free from Fesliyan Studios (fesliyanstudios.com). Built-in voices: sherpa-onnx (Apache 2.0) with Piper voices.

Columns come from each publication’s opinion and analysis sections. Posts are public, from Bluesky and Mastodon; Editrove only sends the accounts you follow and the topics you open.
Alerts within seconds of a newsroom breaking a story, instead of at the next refresh.

Editrove keeps one connection open to Bluesky’s public stream and listens only to the watched newsrooms’ posts (AP, Reuters, AFP, your chosen outlets, and newsrooms in your language). Nothing about you is sent, and there is no Editrove server. Android shows a permanent, silent notification while it runs, and it uses a little more battery and data. Arabic channels aren’t on Bluesky yet, so their breaking news still arrives at each refresh.

Every feature, step by step, with pictures
Everything Editrove can do, one feature at a time. Tap Settings › User guide whenever you need it.

Today opens on Top Stories, put together on your phone from dozens of newsrooms: what editors placed highest and what most outlets are covering, refreshed within minutes. Tap the topic buttons at the top to change topic, choose Curated, Newest or Oldest, and pull down to refresh. The red LIVE strip scrolls the latest headlines.

Tap any story to read it in Editrove’s reader, without ads or clutter. The small and large A buttons make the text smaller or bigger. Summary lists the key points, worked out on your phone. The heart likes a story, the arrows share it (the headline and the newspaper’s own link), and the bookmark saves it. Listen reads the story aloud.

Editrove opens each newspaper the best way it can: from the publisher, through a browser view, or from archive copies. When a story can’t be shown in the app, a button opens it through a reader service. A greyed-out story is locked and has no archive copy yet. To read any link, share it to Editrove from another app, or use Settings › Open a link.
Discover gathers the most important stories across all your topics. Type in the search box to find stories or newspapers.

Audio reads the news like a broadcast, with an opening tune and a voice in your language. Tap Play briefing and keep scrolling: the player stays at the bottom of the screen and on your lock screen. In Settings › Audio briefing you can choose headlines, summaries or full articles, the voice and the speed, and schedule Morning, Afternoon and Evening briefings that arrive as a notification. Phones without Google’s speech engine (Huawei and others) get Editrove’s own voice: it downloads once, about 20 MB, and then works offline. To get Google’s voices on such a phone, Settings › Audio briefing shows where to install them, and Speech engine lets you pick any engine on your phone.

Live shows news channels broadcasting right now. Channels marked LIVE play inside Editrove; tap the full-screen button to watch them large. Channels marked YouTube open their official live page. Use the language buttons to see channels in one language.

Switch to Radio for news stations and the popular stations in your country. Radio keeps playing when the screen is off, with controls on the lock screen. Type a station’s name in the search box to find any station.

Columns and analysis from leading newspapers. Tap Follow next to a writer and their new articles gather in the Following tab. Tap a trending topic to make it a tab. The search box shows writers, columns and posts as you type.
Stories you bookmark are kept here to read later, even without internet.

Settings › Edition sets your country and city; they become your national and local tabs. Tap Use my location, or choose a city. Each country suggests its own newspapers, which you can add with a switch. Return to… takes you back to your previous edition in one tap.

Editrove speaks English, Arabic, French, Spanish and German, separately from your phone’s language. Topics, briefings and alerts change with it. The Language row always also says “Language” in English, so you can always find your way back.

Settings › Sources lists every news source. To add a new one, type the newspaper’s name or website in the search box — for example Al-Ahram or youm7.com. Editrove checks each result right away and only shows ones that work. Tap Add and the newspaper appears in the right tabs. No technical addresses needed.

Turn on Notifications, then tap the bell next to the topics you want. Breaking news alerts come when a newsroom breaks a story or several report it at once. Real-time alerts (optional) arrive within seconds; while they’re on, a small permanent notification shows.
Choose Black Glass (dark), Editorial Paper (light) or follow your phone. Set the text size for every story, the order of stories, and on foldables and tablets, split or full view.
Press and hold an empty spot on your home screen, choose Widgets, then Editrove: the Daily Brief player, Top Stories, or a Topic of Choice.
No ads, no tracking, no accounts. Your settings and saved stories stay on your phone. Settings › Backup & restore saves everything to one file.

The most natural voices come from Google’s free speech app (Speech Services by Google). This phone doesn’t have it. Install it, then download your language’s voice; Editrove switches to it by itself.
Turn on Speech Services by Google
In text-to-speech settings you can choose the preferred engine and download voices. On phones without Google services, Google’s voices may not download; Editrove’s own voice keeps working either way.
